STEP 3b CLEAN: live table is 26 items, resp 1-5, matching the 26-item SCS (Neff 2003) French translation described in the paper. Deposit columns SCS1..SCS26 are NOT in the order of the paper's S2 questionnaire, and nothing in the deposit or supplements says which column is which S2 item within a subscale. (1) S3 (item correlation matrix) is |r| in DEPOSIT column order: 323/325 off-diagonal cells match the live |r| within .005 (exceptions: cells 13-12 .44 vs .55 and 25-13 .37 vs .47; S3 diagonal var for item 13 1.83 vs live 1.64). (2) S1 (factor pattern, deposit numbering) assigns SK={2,11,20,22,26}, SJ={5,10,14,15,25}, CH={7,9,17,23}, I={4,6,12,24}, M={3,16,18,21}, OI={1,8,13,19}; that grouping reproduces the paper's Table 3 exactly: SK sum 14.27 (5.05) alpha .89 vs published 14.27 (5.05) .88; SJ reversed 30-15.77=14.23 (5.03) .85 vs 14.23 (5.03) .85; CH 11.56 (3.64) .74 vs 11.56 (3.64) .74; I reversed 24-12.16=11.84 (4.19) .79 vs 11.84 (4.19) .79; M 12.21 (3.72) .80 vs published 13.81 (3.72) .81 (M mean unreproduced, SD/alpha match). First-PC sign splits the 26 columns 13/13 exactly along S1's positive {SK,CH,M} vs negative {SJ,I,OI} subscales (data stored raw, not reverse-scored). (3) S2's own 'Codage' key (= Neff's canonical key SK 5,12,19,23,26 / SJ 1,8,11,16,21 / CH 3,7,10,15 / I 4,13,18,25 / M 9,14,17,22 / OI 2,6,20,24) applied to SCSk by number gives alphas -0.25/-0.08/-0.06/0.13/0.19/-0.19 and only 2/26 items correlate most with their own subscale (S1 grouping: 19/26). So subscale MEMBERSHIP of every column is pinned, but WITHIN a subscale (5!,5!,4!,4!,4!,4! = 7.96e7 assignments) nothing ties a column to an S2 wording; no simple cyclic/affine/reverse permutation of the S2 order fits (best 11/26 subscale agreement). Assigning text would be a guess.
